overview: Jabil is one of the world's largest electronics manufacturing services (EMS) and design/manufacturing solutions providers, offering engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing services across the full product lifecycle for customers in cloud/AI data center infrastructure, networking, capital equipment, automotive, healthcare, energy, and connected living/digital commerce. The company operates roughly 120 facilities in 30 countries (headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida) and reported FY2026 (fiscal year ended August 31, 2026) net revenue of $36.0 billion. Jabil organizes its business into three reportable segments -- Regulated Industries, Intelligent Infrastructure, and Connected Living and Digital Commerce (renamed Intelligent Devices and Robotics effective FY2027) -- reflecting a growing tilt toward AI/data center infrastructure manufacturing.

business_model.summary: Jabil is a turnkey, outsourced manufacturer: it procures components, assembles and tests products, and provides design/engineering services under customer-specific, dedicated business-unit arrangements. Revenue is largely pass-through of material costs plus labor/overhead margin, so it is a low-margin, high-volume, working-capital-intensive model where profitability depends on capacity utilization and product/segment mix (gross margin ~9.2% in FY2026). Most customer contracts only commit on a quarterly rolling basis, making revenue more transactional/demand-driven than contractually recurring, although many relationships persist for years once a product is designed-in.

revenue_streams.name: Intelligent Infrastructure (AI/cloud/data center infrastructure, networking & comms, capital equipment)
Regulated Industries (automotive & transportation, healthcare & packaging, renewable/energy infrastructure)
Connected Living and Digital Commerce / Intelligent Devices and Robotics (warehouse automation, robotics, connected living, digital commerce)

business_model.customer_type: B2B / large enterprise OEMs; five largest customers ~37% of FY2026 revenue, 76 customers ~90% of revenue
business_model.geographic_mix: 73.1% foreign-source revenue in FY2026 (down from 82.5% in FY2024); manufacturing footprint concentrated in China, Malaysia, Mexico and the U.S.; ~140,000 employees (Asia 72k, Americas 52k, Europe 16k)

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest diversified EMS/DMS providers globally, with particular recent strength in AI/data-center infrastructure manufacturing where Intelligent Infrastructure segment revenue grew 45% YoY in FY2026 on hyperscaler/cloud demand

moat_factors.description: ~120 facilities in 30 countries enable local-for-local manufacturing, centralized procurement, and a single ERP system that gives customers supply-chain visibility and reduces tariff/geopolitical exposure
Most business units serve a single customer with dedicated production lines, engineers, and planners; once a product is designed-in, relocating manufacturing is costly and disruptive for the customer

Electronic, mechanical, optical and experience design capabilities (including silicon photonics, co-packaged optics, OSAT) differentiate Jabil from pure assembly-only competitors and support higher value-add programs like AI infrastructure and power management
Centralized global sourcing and commodity management teams provide better component pricing and availability than smaller competitors
The company explicitly states its manufacturing processes are generally not subject to significant proprietary protection, limiting durable technology-based differentiation

weaknesses: Thin, largely commoditized gross margins (~9%) typical of contract manufacturing
High concentration risk: largest customer ~20% of FY2026 revenue (Intelligent Infrastructure segment), top 5 customers ~37%
Customers generally commit to only one quarter of production, limiting revenue visibility and making capacity planning difficult
Constant competitive threat from customers' own insourcing of manufacturing
Capital- and working-capital-intensive model sensitive to component shortages and inventory obsolescence

growth_drivers: AI and cloud/data center infrastructure build-out: Intelligent Infrastructure segment grew to 50% of FY2026 revenue (from 32% in FY2024), with cloud and data center infrastructure revenue up 33% YoY in FY2026
Electrification and renewable/energy infrastructure demand within Regulated Industries
Power management for AI data centers via the Hanley Energy Group acquisition (closed Jan 2026, ~$725M-$752M)
Healthcare/pharma contract manufacturing expansion via Pharmaceutics International (Pii) acquisition (closed Feb 2025, $309M)
Supply-chain/procurement intelligence capabilities added via Rebound Technologies acquisition ($133M, closed Sept 2025)
Warehouse automation and robotics push, reflected in the FY2027 rename of Connected Living and Digital Commerce to Intelligent Devices and Robotics
Continued bolt-on M&A strategy to diversify end markets and add higher-value engineering capabilities
Capital return program: $1.0B (2026) and $1.5B (2027) share repurchase authorizations plus a quarterly dividend

business.description: Largest customer (reported in Intelligent Infrastructure segment) was ~20% of FY2026 net revenue, up from 16% in FY2025; loss or reduction of this or other top customers would materially hurt results
Nearly half of revenue now tied to AI/cloud/data center capex cycles; a slowdown in hyperscaler spending would disproportionately hit the fastest-growing segment
Most customers commit production volumes only one quarter ahead, creating demand-forecasting risk, excess/obsolete inventory risk, and utilization swings
Ongoing memory component shortage and historical semiconductor shortages can curtail production and raise costs

business.risk: Quality/regulatory compliance at acquired healthcare unit
business.description: In August 2026 Jabil received an FDA Warning Letter related to a March 2026 inspection of the Pii Hunt Valley, Maryland facility; manufacturing at the site has been paused pending remediation

financial.description: Total debt rose to ~$3.98B in FY2026 (from ~$2.88B in FY2025) after issuing new senior notes partly to fund the Hanley acquisition; interest expense rose to $181M in FY2026
Majority of revenue is USD-denominated but labor/utility costs outside the U.S. are in local currencies; hedged but not eliminated
A downgrade would raise borrowing costs on revolving credit facilities and could reduce access to the commercial paper program

regulatory.description: Significant China manufacturing exposure; tariff landscape has shifted rapidly (IEEPA tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court in Feb 2026, refunds being processed) and could change again, affecting costs and customer sourcing decisions
FDA QSR/cGMP requirements and foreign equivalents (EU, China NMPA, Japan) expose the healthcare business to enforcement actions, as illustrated by the 2026 Pii warning letter

regulatory.risk: Global minimum tax (OECD Pillar Two) and U.S. tax law changes
regulatory.description: OBBBA and OECD 15% minimum tax framework could affect effective tax rate over time, though no material impact through FY2026

macro.description: Russia/Ukraine and Middle East conflicts create sub-tier raw material (palladium, neon, aluminum) and logistics risk, plus broader trade-policy uncertainty tied to China
Variable-rate borrowings and increased fixed-rate debt issuance make the company sensitive to rate moves

macro.risk: Valuation/sentiment risk around the AI capex narrative
macro.description: The stock rallied to an all-time high of ~$429 in June 2026 on AI infrastructure enthusiasm before falling roughly 40% to the ~$250-260 range by mid-November 2026 amid valuation resets and AI-spending sustainability concerns, despite a beat-and-raise FY2026 Q4 print and FY2027 guidance

macro_factors.industry_outlook: EMS/contract manufacturing industry outlook is bifurcated: traditional segments (consumer, industrial, connected living) are growing slowly to declining, while AI/data-center infrastructure manufacturing is in a multi-year capex upcycle benefiting Jabil, Flex, Celestica and Foxconn
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical; tied to end-customer capex cycles (cloud/hyperscaler, semiconductor capital equipment, automotive) and prone to inventory destocking/restocking swings
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- working-capital-heavy model plus a mix of fixed and variable-rate debt

recent_developments.event: Closed acquisition of Hanley Energy Group (critical power/energy management for data centers) for approximately $725-752 million to expand AI data-center capabilities
U.S. Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs; Jabil began receiving tariff refunds in FY2026, with no material impact on results
Received an FDA Warning Letter related to a March 2026 inspection of the Pharmaceutics International (Pii) facility in Hunt Valley, Maryland; manufacturing at the site paused pending remediation

Reported Q4/FY2026 results: Q4 revenue ~$10.6B and core EPS $4.40, both above guidance and consensus; FY2026 revenue $35.95B (+20.6% YoY) driven by 45% growth in Intelligent Infrastructure; issued FY2027 guidance of ~$44.5B revenue and $17.55 core EPS; shares fell roughly 6-10% post-earnings despite the beat-and-raise, as investors focused on valuation and the scale of growth needed to hit the new targets

Stock rallied to an all-time high of ~$428.93 (June 17, 2026) on AI infrastructure enthusiasm and multiple analyst price-target increases (targets clustering $425-$482), then retraced roughly 40% to the ~$250-260 range by mid-November 2026 amid broader AI-capex sustainability concerns and valuation resets across the group
Board authorized a new $1.5 billion share repurchase program (the '2027 Share Repurchase Program'), following the $1.0 billion 2026 program authorized in July 2025
Management changes: Andrew Priestley named EVP, Chief Operations Officer; Rafael Renno named SVP, Global Business Units leading the Connected Living & Digital Commerce segment

Connected Living and Digital Commerce segment renamed Intelligent Devices and Robotics to reflect increased emphasis on automation/robotics and more complex engineered solutions (no change to segment composition or financials)

items.notes: Implies ~24% YoY growth off FY2026's $35.95B, driven by continued AI/data-center infrastructure demand; above prior Street consensus of ~$42.2B
Margins expected to be weighted toward the second half as new capacity ramps
Reliant in part on supplier financing of a rapidly growing working-capital base tied to AI infrastructure ramp
Sequential step-down from Q4 FY2026's $10.6B actual as management frames revenue as ~45% H1 / 55% H2 FY2027
A step down from Q4 FY2026 core EPS of $4.40, reflecting segment mix and margin timing

guidance.management_commentary: Management attributed FY2026 strength to accelerating AI-related demand across cloud/data center infrastructure, networking, and capital equipment, and guided FY2027 to continued acceleration, while flagging that healthcare/packaging in the Regulated Industries segment saw some delays in automation equipment and that margins and revenue are expected to be weighted toward the back half of FY2027 as new AI-related capacity comes online.

bull_case: Direct, diversified exposure to the AI/data-center infrastructure capex cycle through the Intelligent Infrastructure segment (50% of FY2026 revenue, +45% YoY), with management guiding to continued acceleration in FY2027
Beat-and-raise track record: FY2026 results and FY2027 guidance both exceeded prior Street consensus, and gross margin has been expanding (8.9% to 9.2%) on favorable Intelligent Infrastructure mix
Diversification across Regulated Industries, Intelligent Infrastructure, and Connected Living/Intelligent Devices and Robotics segments cushions against a downturn in any single end market

Bolt-on M&A (Hanley Energy, Pii, Rebound Technologies) is adding higher-value, less-commoditized capabilities (power management, pharma CDMO, procurement intelligence) that can improve the margin mix over time
Significant capital return program ($1.5B repurchase authorization for FY2027 plus a dividend) and improving adjusted free cash flow generation (~$1.37B FY2026, guided ~$1.6B FY2027)
Roughly 40% pullback from the June 2026 all-time high may have reset valuation to a more attractive entry point relative to still-growing AI-infrastructure revenue
bear_case: Thin, commodity-like EMS margins mean results are highly sensitive to utilization, component costs, and customer mix; core operating margin guided at only ~6.1% for FY2027

Heavy and growing reliance on a single large customer (~20% of FY2026 revenue) and on the sustainability of AI/hyperscaler capital spending; any slowdown would hit the fastest-growing, now-largest segment

Stock has already shown extreme volatility (all-time high ~$429 in June 2026 to ~$250-260 by November 2026), suggesting the market is actively re-rating AI-capex-linked names and that sentiment, not just fundamentals, is driving the shares
Rising debt load (total debt up to ~$3.98B in FY2026 from ~$2.88B) and higher interest expense from recent senior notes issuances used to fund acquisitions

Regulatory/quality risk realized in the healthcare vertical: FDA Warning Letter and paused manufacturing at the Pii Hunt Valley facility in 2026 highlights execution risk in less-commoditized, higher-margin acquisitions
Significant foreign-sourced revenue (73% in FY2026) and China manufacturing exposure leave the business exposed to an unpredictable global tariff landscape and geopolitical shocks
